utility.notes: Austin Energy is a municipally-owned (city-owned) electric utility — the sole electric provider across most of the City of Austin.

value.name: Austin Energy
value.notes: Because Austin Energy is a municipal utility, the City of Austin and the utility are effectively the same government entity for solar purposes: city building permits and utility interconnection review both route through the same Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) portal, per Austin Energy's own May 2026 Solar Permitting Manual.

county.notes: Austin's municipal boundary extends into parts of Williamson and Hays counties as well, but a single City government (Austin Development Services) and a single municipal utility (Austin Energy) administer permitting and interconnection citywide regardless of county line.

permit_authority.value: City of Austin Development Services (ADS) / Building and Trade Contractor Services (BTCS), in coordination with Austin Energy
permit_authority.notes: Per Austin Energy's own Solar Permitting Manual (published May 2026): all Solar Distributed Generation (DG) systems and Energy Storage Systems in Austin Energy territory require an Auxiliary Power Electrical Permit, submitted through the same Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) portal used for other City permits. Ground-mount and building-integrated (solar-shingle) systems inside city limits additionally require CoA Residential Plan Review with a corresponding Building Permit, under which the Auxiliary Power EP falls, allowing Austin Energy to perform the DG system inspection as part of the same City-integrated process.

interconnection_url.notes: Confirmed directly from Austin Energy's own rate page: the Value of Solar (VoS) rate is 9.91 cents/kWh for systems under 1MW-AC (7.24 cents/kWh at or above 1MW-AC), effective March 1, 2023, and updated every three years as an average of the five previous years' assessments. This is NOT traditional net metering — Austin Energy meters and credits 100% of solar production at the VoS rate, while separately billing the customer for all electricity consumed, rather than netting production against consumption 1:1. Credits apply only to electric charges (not water, solid waste, etc.) and roll forward indefinitely but are non-transferable.

battery_programs.notes: Austin Energy's own Solar Permitting Manual references a separate incentive-application system (EECP, Energy Efficiency Collaboration Platform) that contractors use to enter Austin Energy incentives, including presumably for Energy Storage Systems, but no specific battery incentive dollar figure was independently confirmed this session.

value.name: Distributed Generation Planning Application (DGPA)
value.required_when: always, required for all Auxiliary Power EPs

value.name: Wire diagram / design packet for the proposed system design
Residential Interconnection Agreement
value.required_when: always, required for all Residential DG projects prior to permit activation

value.name: Engineer-stamped plan sets, plus a corresponding Building Permit
value.required_when: ground-mounted systems and building-integrated photovoltaic (solar-shingle) systems located inside Austin city limits

required_documents.notes: Per Austin Energy's own May 2026 Solar Permitting Manual. A rooftop-mounted, non-shingle residential system inside Austin city limits or within the ETJ needs only the Residential Auxiliary Power EP (DGPA, wire diagram, Interconnection Agreement) and does not require a separate City building permit.

value: Once the permit reaches 'Active' status, the contractor requests a solar inspection through the Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) portal's 'My Inspections' tab
A pre-construction meeting is optional for residential projects (required for commercial); once requested, a Final solar inspection cannot be scheduled until the pre-construction meeting is complete
All other related permits (e.g. Repair/Upgrade EPs) must be in 'Final' status before a Final Auxiliary Power EP inspection can be scheduled

After the Final inspection passes, Austin Energy's Distributed Metering Operations (AE DMO) team installs the solar meter(s) on site and updates the permit to 'Final' status, at which point the customer receives Permission to Operate (PTO)

value.notes: No single confirmed end-to-end permit review timeline was published in Austin Energy's own May 2026 Solar Permitting Manual. Confirmed component timings: once an inspection is requested, it is typically formally scheduled by the AE Solar Inspections team within 3 business days; after the final inspection passes, meter installation and Permission to Operate typically follow within about 1 week, per the manual's own example notification email; and after PTO, the $4,000 rebate check is mailed within 7-10 business days following Quality Assurance review, per Austin Energy's own rebate page.

value.program_or_pathway: Residential Auxiliary Power Electrical Permit (EP) via the Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) portal; ground-mount and building-integrated (solar-shingle) systems inside city limits additionally require Residential Plan Review with a corresponding Building Permit.
other_conditions: Systems installed within Austin's ETJ (extraterritorial jurisdiction) or outside city limits still need a Residential Auxiliary Power EP, but do not require a City of Austin building permit.
An Interconnection Agreement is required for all Residential DG projects before permit activation.

Austin Energy conducts its own additional internal Distributed Generation review whenever proposed DG output is 25kW-AC or greater, when interconnecting to the Downtown Network, when the system is an interconnected spinning generator, or when it includes an Energy Storage System — the 25kW figure recorded above is this internal-review trigger, not necessarily a hard interconnection cap.
The Value of Solar (VoS) rate applies instead of traditional 1:1 net metering (see interconnection_url notes).

permit_fees.notes: Austin Energy's own manual states the permit 'will auto-bill fees' once approved, payable by the assigned Electrical Contractor, but does not publish a specific dollar figure or fee schedule — left null rather than using unverified numbers from third-party sources.

value.name: Austin Energy Residential Solar Rebate
value.description: A rebate for eligible home solar installations, paid by check after the system passes final inspection, receives Permission to Operate, and clears Austin Energy's Quality Assurance review.
value.eligibility: Requires an active Austin Energy residential electric account at the premise, a new system of 3kW (DC) or larger that is mostly free of shading, installation by an Austin Energy participating contractor, and signed Residential Interconnection Agreement and Customer Agreement Form. Third-party Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) are prohibited in Austin Energy territory and are not eligible.

rebates.notes: Confirmed directly from Austin Energy's own residential solar rebate page. This $4,000 figure (fetched directly this session) supersedes an older $2,500 figure that appears in some third-party search-indexed summaries.
